title: Offset, PSRR and Noise of Op Amps
intro: Real op amps have a floor on precision set by offset, supply sensitivity and noise.

items: Input offset: a mismatch between the two sides produces an output at zero differential input; referred to the input it is a few mV random plus systematic offset. Large input devices reduce random offset (about 1/sqrt(W*L)).
Input common-mode range: the pair and the tail source must stay saturated. A rail-to-rail input uses parallel NMOS and PMOS pairs.

PSRR: the ratio of the gain from input to output to the gain from supply to output. It degrades at high frequency because capacitances couple the supply into the output; a fully differential design improves it.
Noise: input-referred thermal noise is dominated by the first stage and falls as 1/gm1; flicker noise by device area.

blocks.text: These specifications together determine the 'resolution' of a signal chain; a 12-bit converter's front end, for example, needs input noise well below one LSB and offset below its dynamic range.

blocks.title: Offset and area
blocks.text: A pair has random offset of 4 mV for W*L = 10 um^2. What area gives 1 mV?
solution: Offset scales as 1/sqrt(W*L). To cut it by 4 times, area must grow by 16: 160 um^2.
